empty_hint: When one of your processes dumps core, it shows up here.
err_poll: coredumpctl did not answer, see the Noctalia log
err_uid: Could not resolve the user id, crash list disabled
journal_empty: Nothing at this level in the current boot
notify_body: {signal}, PID {pid} — open the Crashes panel to diagnose

agent_cmd.description: Command that receives the diagnosis prompt as its last argument: "claude", "codex", "opencode --prompt", "grok --"… Empty = use the first installed well-known agent.
agent_cmd.label: AI agent command

agent_order.description: Which agents to try and in what order, e.g. "codex, claude". Empty: claude, opencode, codex, grok.
agent_order.label: Agent order

env_file.description: Sourced before the agent starts. For a proxy or an API key your shell sets but a panel click does not inherit, e.g. ~/.config/agent-env.
env_file.label: Environment file

extra_prompt.description: Text appended to every diagnosis prompt — e.g. "Answer in Russian" or house rules for the agent.
extra_prompt.label: Extra prompt

notify.description: Announce new crashes of your processes with a critical notification. Turn off if something else already announces them.
notify.label: Desktop notifications

poll_seconds.description: How often to re-read the systemd-coredump journal.
poll_seconds.label: Poll interval (seconds)

probe_agent.description: Before opening the window, ask the agent a throwaway question; if it cannot answer — out of quota, logged out, offline — the next one is opened instead. Costs one tiny request per diagnosis. Off: the first installed agent is opened whether or not it works.
probe_agent.label: Check the agent can answer

terminal_cmd.description: Wrapper that opens the agent in a window, e.g. "kitty -e". Leave empty if the agent command opens its own window.
terminal_cmd.label: Terminal command

tip_diagnose: Diagnose with AI in a terminal
tip_no_core: The core dump is gone (rotated away) — nothing to analyze
title: Crashes
